title: The gift you didn't see coming
old_caption: Getting a gift when you have nothing to give back can set off a quiet panic. A real thank you is enough. If you want to give later, let it come from the heart, not the pressure.

title: When the day goes sideways
old_caption: When the big day goes sideways, it's easy to feel like you ruined it. Laugh first, lower the bar to simply being together, and name one thing that went right.

title: The day-after slump
old_caption: The quiet after the holidays can hit harder than you expect. Give yourself one slow day, get outside for a few minutes, and put one small, nice plan on the calendar.

title: The New Year's plan
old_caption: Wanting a big night when your person wants pajamas isn't a problem to win. Say what you really want, find the overlap, and build a plan you both actually like.

title: The year-end check-in
old_caption: Before the year ends, try three questions together: your favourite moment, what was hard, and what you want more of. Listen to the hard one gently. Save this for a cozy night in.

title: You made it
old_caption: If the holidays left you tired, you're not doing it wrong. You held boundaries, asked for help, and were gentle with yourself. Rest is allowed, and you made it.

title: Aries in December: then vs now
old_caption: Then: seven parties a night, every night. Now: one night circled REST, on purpose. Rest is on the calendar now.

title: Taurus's holiday dinner: then vs now
old_caption: Midnight dinner alone by the fridge light, or a big pot and a full table? Good food tastes better shared.

title: Gemini's holiday texts: then vs now
old_caption: Twelve chats, three typing at once, nobody really talking. Then one long call. One real call beats twelve half-chats.

title: Cancer homesick: then vs now
old_caption: "I'm fine!!" with a wobbly lip, versus "I miss home" said out loud. Saying it lets the people around you help.
